body:
N992-xh1-reaction-qualified-progression-proposal | A covalent product receipt is proposed to gate reaction-qualified molecular progression

STATUS | High-level proposal from a captured response, retained only as a nonprocedural curator summary. No integrated chemistry, measured kinetics or working correctness gate is acquired.

PROPOSAL
The response proposes that a covalent product-state receipt could authorize progression to a later nucleic-acid-addressed instruction. It names an azide-locked progression concept and credits earlier product-state reading, staged or autonomous DNA-directed synthesis, and fuel-driven nucleic-acid association/turnover as antecedents. The proposed combination is not shown to operate as a repeatable chemical progression.

FAILURE MODES AND OPEN REQUIREMENTS
The summary identifies false receipts from nonproductive or wrong-site joining, product integrity and stereochemistry, linker/address integrity, side reactions, accumulated nucleic-acid bulk, recovery, throughput and cost. A shared chemical environment is proposed but not demonstrated. No general molecular correctness gate, physical operation, novelty, priority or practical advantage is established.

RELATION TO EXISTING XH1 RECORDS
This is a progression-gating proposal, distinct from N988's downstream filtering of a completed genotype-linked library. It does not establish a reliable receipt or remove N989's exact empty-carrier observation alias; the earlier two-state counterexample remains valid within its stated transition/observation model.

SOURCE LIMIT
Only the sanitized curator extract is included in the public intake. The captured RESPONSE.md is identified by exact hash and size in that extract and remains in its local source receipt. No sequences, reagent combinations, concentrations, reaction conditions or procedures are reproduced.

EVIDENCE
The retained source is a curator summary of a captured response, not original workspace-file bytes. Its proposals and limits remain source-reported.

review.scope: Source-supported extraction only; scoped substantive acceptance requires a separate version-bound review overlay.
